sentence: This project studies compounds that make glioblastoma cells turn neuron-like in response to radiation, to make radiation treatment work better.
This project studies why muscle weakness happens in myotonic dystrophy, focusing on how muscle handles calcium.
This project does genetic testing of a colony of rhesus macaques, including genes of the major histocompatibility complex that shape how animals respond to infection.
This project follows a large group of people over time to find out which state and local conditions relate to HIV infection and to using HIV prevention tools.
This project builds a computer method that finds biological subtypes of psychiatric disorders using human brain imaging data, and applies it to autism.
This project studies how beta amyloid affects neurons, testing whether it helps them communicate, using genetically engineered human neurons.
This project studies phage satellites in Mycobacterium aichiense, asking how they use genes, work with helper phages, and spread across bacterial species.
This project tries to find out how transposable elements move within genomes and between species, and how genomes stay intact.
This project tests rhesus macaques in a colony for genes of the major histocompatibility complex and for several viruses, while keeping the colony genetically diverse.
This project studies how Salmonella survives sulfites made by activated neutrophils, by mapping the transcriptional pathways that help it resist them.
This project builds lab models to test drugs for endometriosis, adenomyosis, heavy menstrual bleeding and polycystic ovary syndrome, with a focus on the liver.
This project studies nuclear mitochondrial insertions in human genomes, looking for changes in the cortex and other tissues using sequencing and computer methods.
This project looks for anti-cancer drugs that help T cells work better in tumors, using drug screens and single-cell CRISPR screening.
This project studies how the brain's background activity forms patterns, and how those patterns change in psychiatric and neurological disorders.
This project tests treatments that target damaged senescent blood-forming stem cells, to improve bone marrow function in sickle cell disease.
This project studies how genomic sequencing at birth can be used well, including how families, clinicians and labs handle the results over time.
This project tests whether diffusion MRI and resting-state functional MRI can measure how a drug treatment changes Alzheimer's disease in a mouse model.
This project uses electronic medical records and artificial intelligence to build a tool that predicts how patients with severe lung infection respond to early treatment.
This project studies the causes of Alzheimer's disease and related dementias, and works on ways to diagnose and treat the disease early.
